text:
maria_cs: forwarding a customer report — they moved traffic to an interface endpoint yesterday and now see intermittent 502s + TLS failures when calling our /v1/generate endpoint. they say it works from a bastion but not from app pods. logs from customer below, quoting.

maria_cs: customer paste: "curl -v https://api.redwood-infer.internal/v1/generate 
* Rebuilt URL to: https://api.redwood-infer.internal/v1/generate/
*   Trying 10.0.5.23...
* TCP_NODELAY set
* Connected to api.redwood-infer.internal (10.0.5.23) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.2 connection using TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256
* server certificate verification OK
* TLS: initial handshake completed in 150 ms
> GET /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood-infer.internal
> User-Agent: curl/7.78.0
> Accept: */*
< HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
< content-type: text/html
< content-length: 560

We also see, in the app logs, repeated connection resets and a spike in retries leading to a billing spike."

alex_support: thanks — few quick asks: can you paste the app-side curl -v (from failing pod) and a short tcpdump (first 1MB) capturing the handshake? also confirm whether they put a proxy on the path (squid/nginx) or any IPS.

maria_cs: they provided a pod curl -v: 
"curl -v https://api.redwood-infer.internal/v1/generate 
*   Trying 10.0.5.23...
* Connected to 10.0.5.23 (10.0.5.23) port 443 (#0)
* schannel: next InitializeSecurityContext failed: Unknown error (0x80092012) - The revocation function was unable to check revocation for the certificate.
* Closing connection 0
curl: (35) schannel: next InitializeSecurityContext failed: Unknown error (0x80092012) - The revocation function was unable to check revocation for the certificate."

lee_sre: interesting — the bastion verified the cert but the pod failed with cert revocation check. two hypotheses: 1) DNS inside cluster resolves api.redwood-infer.internal to a local proxy/ALB that terminates TLS and presents a different cert (missing SAN for api.redwood-infer.internal), or 2) egress path from pods goes through a network appliance that blocks OCSP/CRL lookups so schannel can't check revocation.

mike_infra: also check endpoint policy and route table on the interface endpoint: if they restricted outbound to specific CIDRs we might be getting hit by a cross-account proxy or ALB that rewrites Host/SNI. ask for the TLS server cert chain (openssl s_client -showcerts -connect 10.0.5.23:443 -servername api.redwood-infer.internal) from both bastion and failing pod (if possible).

maria_cs: customer ran openssl from bastion: 
"openssl s_client -showcerts -connect 10.0.5.23:443 -servername api.redwood-infer.internal 
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=2 O = Digital Org, CN = DigiCA Root
verify return:1
subject=/CN=load-proxy.company.internal
issuer=/CN=DigiCA Root
---
Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=load-proxy.company.internal
   i:/CN=DigiCA Root
---
"

maria_cs: and from a pod (busybox) they can't run openssl; they attached a tcpdump pcap (first 400KB). attaching link to s3 copy: https://s3.redwood-internal/support-uploads/2754318000/handshake.pcap (customer provided)

alex_support: thanks — the cert subject for the bastion shows CN=load-proxy.company.internal — so an internal load-proxy is terminating TLS. that's probably why the pod sees revocation failures or different TLS behavior. if the proxy isn't passing through SNI or is replacing certs we get 502s from our upstream.

lee_sre: quick checklist for customers who see this pattern: allow outbound OCSP/CRL endpoints (80/443 to CRL/OCSP servers), confirm interface endpoint policy doesn't restrict egress to a NAT-only path that hops through a TLS-terminating appliance, ensure security groups allow ephemeral ports from connection initiator to return traffic (1024-65535). Also verify conditional DNS: if they enabled private DNS for the endpoint, ensure it resolves to our interface endpoint IPs across all subnets the pods use.

mike_infra: from the pcap we can see the client sends SNI "api.redwood-infer.internal" but the server immediately responds with a cert for "load-proxy.company.internal" and a TCP reset after the proxy's backend returns 502 html. so it's a transparent TLS-terminating proxy in the egress path.

alex_support: recommended repro steps for customer — (1) from a failing pod, nslookup api.redwood-infer.internal and record the A record; (2) curl -v --resolve api.redwood-infer.internal:443:<bastion-ip> https://api.redwood-infer.internal/v1/generate to force connect to the bastion IP (should succeed) — this will tell us if resolution is the issue; (3) temporarily allow OCSP/CRL egress and re-test; (4) if using endpoint policy, open a cidr to permit our public egress to bypass proxy, or make a direct route to interface endpoint.

maria_cs: customer tried --resolve to the bastion ip and it works from the pod (200 OK). they also confirmed after adding a temporary egress allow for ocsp and 80/443 to internet the schannel error goes away.

lee_sre: that nails it — proxy was intercepting TLS and either not providing proper OCSP stapling or blocking the revocation check. two options: 1) update proxy to allow passthrough to our endpoint IPs for TLS (SNI passthrough) and let TLS terminate at our side, or 2) install customer-managed certs on proxy with proper SANs and OCSP stapling (not ideal). recommend option 1 for minimal changes.

mike_infra: also callout routing: if they used a TGW/central egress NAT that hairpins to a different AZ, the interface endpoint private IP may not be reachable from the pod's AZ unless you associate endpoint subnets with the pod subnets. recommend verifying interface endpoint ENI placement and route tables.

alex_support: next actions — I've asked customer to: 1) update proxy to passthrough SNI for api.redwood-infer.internal OR open direct egress to our interface endpoint IPs; 2) revert the temporary allowlist and instead add explicit App -> endpoint subnet route; 3) send updated pcap and confirm error gone. I'll monitor for billing/retry spikes and issue a credit if the retries caused a measurable billing impact. :thumbsup:

maria_cs: customer will try changes this afternoon and post results. tagging ops-bot to capture timeline.

ops-bot: noted incident 2026-03-17T15:10Z — created support case SC-8812, assigned to alex_support/lee_sre.

alex_support: thanks — follow-up pending, will update thread when customer confirms. :thinking:
